title: PDF Solutions CONNECT 2026 Trip Report
gist: Trip report from PDF Solutions' CONNECT 2026, centered on Exensio Aurora, a new server-side analytics architecture PDFS says gives ~25x internal performance gains at comparable hardware spend. PDFS pitches LLM-built, reusable and auditable analytical workflows plus cross-supply-chain connectivity (secureWISE, Sapience) as the way AI actually creates value in fabs, against a backdrop where under 5% of manufacturing data is analyzed.

insights.claim: PDF Solutions (NASDAQ: PDFS) rests on three pillars feeding one data layer: Exensio analytics, Cimetrix/SecureWise equipment connectivity, and DirectScan/Design-for-Inspection on-chip and eBeam measurement.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Diversified data-acquisition plus analytics stack makes PDFS more than a software vendor.
insights.quote: Today, its business rests on three pillars, all feeding a single data layer

insights.claim: The author argues the connectivity layer (Cimetrix plus the March 2025 SecureWise acquisition) is what turns PDF Solutions into a manufacturing data aggregator rather than just an analytics vendor.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Data-aggregation position across fabs and OEMs is a structural moat worth valuing separately from analytics revenue.
insights.quote: The connectivity layer is what makes PDFS a manufacturing data aggregator, not just an analytics vendor.

insights.claim: DirectScan/eBeam inspection is framed as PDF Solutions' differentiated-data moat: it generates proprietary characterization data at advanced nodes that optical inspection cannot see, then monetizes analytics on top.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Proprietary data generation at leading nodes is harder to replicate than analytics software.

insights.claim: PDF Solutions reports about 350 customers spanning fabs, fabless companies, OSATs and equipment OEMs, positioning it as a broker of data across the semiconductor chain.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Neutral, cross-chain position supports network effects in data sharing.
insights.quote: The company reports about 350 customers spanning fabs, fabless, OSATs and equipment OEMs

insights.claim: Samsung's metrology and inspection director presented on adopting PDF Solutions' DirectScan to ramp leading-edge chips, and Intel presented on moving its manufacturing data infrastructure to AI-driven analytics with PDF.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Tier-1 customer endorsements of DirectScan and Exensio signal real adoption at leading-edge IDMs/foundries.
insights.locator: Customer speakers and what they were billed to cover

insights.claim: PDF Solutions says that in its experience under 5% of semiconductor manufacturing data gets analyzed with traditional tools, while 3D architectures, advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration drive a data explosion that blurs front-end/back-end boundaries.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Large untapped analytics headroom underpins the TAM argument for Aurora.
insights.quote: in its experience under 5% of semiconductor manufacturing data gets analyzed with traditional tools

insights.claim: Exensio Aurora was built because conventional BI tools hit in-memory processing limits and general-purpose cloud data platforms lack semiconductor relevance, and customers pushed for it.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Positions PDFS against generic cloud data platforms on domain specificity.
insights.quote: conventional BI tools hit in-memory processing limits and general-purpose cloud data platforms lack semiconductor relevance

insights.claim: CTO Kimon Michaels reported roughly 25-fold performance improvements for Aurora in internal testing at comparable hardware spending, though the figures are company-reported and workload dependent.
insights.speaker: Kimon Michaels
insights.so_what: A large efficiency claim that still needs independent validation before being underwritten.
insights.quote: Michaels reported approximately 25-fold performance improvements in internal testing at comparable hardware spending.

insights.claim: A trade outlet cautioned that the September Aurora announcement defined architecture and direction rather than offering an independently benchmarked production result.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Treat Aurora performance claims as unproven until customer production benchmarks appear.
insights.quote: the September announcement defined the architecture and direction rather than offering an independently benchmarked production result
insights.locator: One trade outlet noted the caveat

insights.claim: Aurora shifts heavy analysis from desktop clients to distributed server-side computation via its FUSE computing stack, which handles both parallel processing and parallel data access, with caching of reusable intermediate results.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Server-side architecture shift could drive larger, stickier enterprise deployments.
insights.quote: Aurora shifts heavy analysis from desktop clients to distributed server-side computation.

insights.claim: Aurora expands manufacturing history beyond flat tables, keeping repeated measurements, retests, derived values and wafer/die/assembly relationships connected, and integrating design and product-lifecycle data.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Graph-like data modeling is a prerequisite for chiplet-era traceability.

insights.claim: CEO John Kibarian argues AI hardware demand is constrained by equipment availability, energy and manufacturing capacity, so customers must extract more output from existing resources even while adding capacity.
insights.speaker: John Kibarian
insights.so_what: Capacity scarcity raises the value of yield and utilization software.
insights.quote: Demand for AI hardware is growing, but equipment availability, energy and manufacturing capacity constrain production.

insights.claim: Kibarian observes that bespoke chips from foundation-model companies and data-center operators create more products with potentially smaller production runs, and some customers effectively never leave new product introduction.
insights.speaker: John Kibarian
insights.so_what: Custom-silicon proliferation increases per-product data and analytics intensity, a tailwind for PDFS.
insights.quote: Some customers, Kibarian observed, effectively never leave new product introduction
insights.locator: More products and more complex data

insights.claim: Advanced packaging, photonics and co-packaged optics, plus fabless firms juggling multiple manufacturing partners and test stages, make traceability and data integration increasingly important.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Back-end complexity expands the addressable market for cross-supply-chain data platforms.
insights.locator: Assembly and test are also becoming

insights.claim: Kibarian describes LLMs' practical role as constructing analytical workflows (query, calculate, plot, annotate blocks in Python with visual sequences) that engineers can inspect, execute and reuse.
insights.speaker: John Kibarian
insights.so_what: Frames LLMs as workflow builders rather than answer engines, a defensible enterprise pattern.
insights.quote: constructing analytical workflows that engineers can inspect, execute and reuse

insights.claim: Storing validated workflows reduces repeated model interactions and compute cost while preserving engineering knowledge and enabling audit of how a screening decision was reached.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Reusability lowers inference costs and meets auditability needs for long-life products like automotive.
insights.locator: Once validated, a workflow can be stored

insights.claim: PDF Solutions argues general-purpose AI models miss relationships among products, tools, chambers and process histories that experienced engineers understand, so manufacturing data must be combined with semiconductor-specific context.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Domain context is positioned as the moat against generic AI platforms.
insights.quote: An experienced engineer understands relationships among products, tools, chambers and process histories that a general-purpose AI model may miss.

insights.claim: Exensio StudioAI handles model development, deployment, monitoring and governance, with time-critical algorithms running on testers or tools and less urgent work running centrally or in the cloud, on an open architecture supporting customers' own models and agents.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Edge-to-cloud model governance expands PDFS's role into MLOps for fabs.

insights.claim: PDF Solutions is extending secureWISE's encrypted fab-to-equipment-supplier collaboration toward fabless companies and OSATs, while Sapience Manufacturing Hub links manufacturing data to enterprise processes.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Broadening the connectivity network could expand PDFS's data footprint and cross-sell.
insights.quote: PDF Solutions is extending that connectivity toward fabless companies and outsourced assembly and test providers.

insights.claim: The author concludes AI's value in semiconductor manufacturing will be measured by faster diagnosis, better equipment utilization and production decisions engineers can understand and trust.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Investor KPI lens for fab-AI vendors: diagnosis speed and utilization, not model novelty.
insights.quote: AI’s value in semiconductor manufacturing will be measured by faster diagnosis, better equipment utilization and production decisions that engineers can understand and trust.
insights.locator: A successful event with a clear direction
